solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Models succeeded in what fashion with men?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
'in what fashion?' asks how
chessmen are also called pieces

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at how catwalk models made it in fashion alongside male models.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' here are the pieces on a chessboard, not male models.
explanation.definitionFit: Showpieces are prime examples put on display, as models of their kind are.

clue.text: Absorbs with interest what all across answers here have

definitions.meaning: to drink in a sight or story is to take it in eagerly

definitions.text: what all across answers here have
definitions.meaning: every across answer contains a drink: CHAR has char (tea), TRUMP CARDS rum, TWINED wine, GINSBERG gin, SKIRTS kir, OSTEAL tea, DALE ale and so on

explanation.surface: Someone soaks up details, then the clue nods to a theme running through the across lights.
explanation.walkthrough: Look through the across answers: each hides a drink, e.g. RUM in TRUMP CARDS, PORT in CONTACT SPORTS, FANTA in INFANTAS, POP in ANTIPOPE, ROSE in BED OF ROSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink in is an idiom for absorbing something attentively; the second reading is literal, drinks contained in words.

clue.text: Heavy food, say, Dorothy's thrown up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: EG (for example) stands for 'say'
Dot is short for Dorothy, so Dorothy's gives DOT'S, written DOTS

explanation.surface: Dorothy has eaten something stodgy and been sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown up' looks like vomiting, but in a down clue it reverses EGDOTS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is filling, starchy food that sits heavily in the stomach.

clue.text: Cat climbing around summit isn't shy

indicators.note: around means the reversed cat goes round the summit word
in a down clue, climbing means the word for cat is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: puss is an everyday word for a cat
a peak is a mountain summit

explanation.surface: A cat scrambling round a mountain top is no shrinking violet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' means reading upwards, so the cat is written backwards before 'around' wraps it round the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who speaks up voices opinions openly, the opposite of keeping quiet out of shyness.

clue.text: Tropical area close to coast in Haiti possibly

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so this takes the final letter of coast
possibly signals that the letters of Haiti may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A tropical place near the shore in Haiti, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but means the last letter of 'coast', T; 'possibly' rearranges HAITI to AHITI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is an island in French Polynesia in the South Pacific, inside the tropics.

clue.text: Python not given to exertion

definitions.meaning: Eric ... was a member of the Monty Python comedy team

explanation.surface: A snake that cannot be bothered to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Python' looks like the snake, but it is the comedy troupe, whose members included Eric Idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Monty Python member's surname, and an adjective for a lazy person who avoids work.

clue.text: Burn a lot of the vegetable

indicators.note: a lot of but not all of a word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: Scorching much of the greens in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' means most of CHARD, losing its final D.
explanation.definitionFit: To char is to scorch or blacken something by burning.

clue.text: What players want is president's entertaining wit

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the president's name contains the wit

parts.note: Trump is a US president, so president's gives TRUMP'S, written TRUMPS
a card is an amusing, witty person

explanation.surface: Players hope for the president's witty, entertaining remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' looks like 'amusing', but it means playing host: the president's name holds the wit within it.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games players hope to be dealt trumps, the strongest suit; a trump card is any decisive advantage.

clue.text: Ugly quality of a French blind that keeps cool

parts.note: un is French for 'a'

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so the blind word contains the cool word

parts.note: sightless means blind
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: An unattractive feature of a French window blind that stays cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blind' suggests a window shade, but it is the adjective meaning unable to see; 'that keeps' puts the cool word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightliness is the state of being unpleasant to look at, i.e. ugliness.

clue.text: What Victor gets, punching Theodore, is wound

indicators.note: the victor's prize punches into, so goes inside, the name

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Theodore
a victor gets a win

explanation.surface: A man named Victor punches Theodore and is left wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is not an injury but the past tense of wind, as in twisting thread.
explanation.definitionFit: Twined means twisted or coiled round, which is what wound (from wind) also means.

clue.text: Having diseased joints, son put out flags around home

indicators.note: around means the flags word goes round the home word

parts.note: to lay flagstones is to pave, so put out flags gives paved
in means at home

explanation.surface: A son decorates the house with bunting while suffering from arthritic joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' suggests bunting, but they are flagstones, and laying them is paving; 'around' wraps that round the home word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spavin is a disease of a horse's hock joint, so a spavined animal has diseased joints.

clue.text: Sing works by composer or poet

indicators.note: works as a verb means stirs or kneads, so the letters of sing are worked into a new order

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Choral works by a composer or settings of a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a noun for compositions; it is the anagram signal turning SING into GINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was an American Beat poet, author of Howl.

clue.text: Avoids satirical performances about queen

indicators.note: about means the performances word goes round the queen's letter

parts.note: skits are short satirical sketches
R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: Someone steers clear of satirical shows mocking the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go round its edge and so evade it.

clue.text: E-car manufacturer with cold lubricants in transformers

parts.note: Tesla makes electric cars
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
oils are lubricants

explanation.surface: An electric-car maker uses cold lubricants inside its transformers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tesla coil is a resonant transformer that produces very high voltages.

clue.text: Wear boring visual aids for activities such as rugby

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the wear word goes inside the visual aids

parts.note: contacts (contact lenses) help eyesight
to sport something is to wear it

explanation.surface: Wearing dull glasses for playing rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like 'dull', but means going inside; 'visual aids' are lenses, not slides.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a contact sport, one where players physically tackle each other; this is an example definition.

clue.text: Exclusively for the FT, hosting loud card game

indicators.note: hosting means holding a guest within, so the phrase contains the loud letter

parts.note: from the newspaper's own viewpoint, something exclusively for the FT is 'all ours'
F (forte) is the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: An exclusive newspaper story about a noisy card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the Financial Times itself, so something just for it is ALL OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: All fours is an old English trick-taking game played with cards.

clue.text: Magritte, say, capturing aged, decrepit deserter

indicators.note: capturing means holding prisoner within, so the painter's name contains the rearranged letters

parts.note: René Magritte, the Belgian surrealist, is an example of someone named René

indicators.note: decrepit means broken down, so the letters of aged are jumbled

explanation.surface: The surrealist painter captures an old, frail runaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrepit' rearranges the clue's 'aged' into EGAD, and 'capturing' puts that inside the painter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is one who abandons a cause, side or faith, a turncoat.

clue.text: Huge duck is perhaps bony

parts.note: OS (outsize) is the clothing abbreviation for huge
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A big duck turns out to be all bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' hedges the definition: osteal means relating to or resembling bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is a technical adjective meaning of bone or bone-like.

clue.text: Boss withdrawing current soldiers

indicators.note: a tide withdrawing ebbs back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A boss pulls out the soldiers under current orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawing' applies only to the current, like an ebbing sea; the soldiers follow unreversed. OR (other ranks) is the usual crossword soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor runs a newspaper or magazine, so is its boss.

clue.text: Trendy wishful thinking mostly for princesses

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a fantasy is wishful thinking

explanation.surface: Fashionable daydreams are mostly about being a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantas are daughters of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch, i.e. princesses.

clue.text: Polish, perhaps, is European language that's spoken

indicators.note: spoken means said aloud, so the language name gives a word sounding the same

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Polish is a European language, perhaps, and one that's spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language from Poland; it is the lowercase sense, a gloss or coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the final surface treatment of something, of which a polish is one kind.

clue.text: A refusal to admit hint for religious leader's rival

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the refusal word contains the hint

parts.note: nope is a casual refusal
a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: A refusal to let a churchman's rival be suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a claimant set up in opposition to the legitimately elected pope.

clue.text: Winter holiday in Spanish region to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: León is a region in north-west Spain

explanation.surface: A winter break taken in a northern part of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is another name for Christmas, the midwinter festival.

clue.text: Show agreement to eat sticky stuff that's lousy

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the agreement word swallows the sticky stuff

parts.note: to nod is to show agreement
goo is sticky stuff

explanation.surface: Nodding along while eating something sticky and unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for worthless or very poor in quality.

clue.text: Swilling beers with food's a pleasant experience

indicators.note: swilling liquid sloshes it around, so these letters are swirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Knocking back beer with food is a pleasant time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a bed of roses' means an easy, comfortable situation.

clue.text: One seeking to exterminate endless depression

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a Dalek, from the TV series Doctor Who, shouts 'Exterminate!'

explanation.surface: A would-be killer driven by endless depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Daleks are the robot-like aliens in the BBC's Doctor Who, famous for screeching 'Exterminate!'; 'endless' drops the K.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, a depression in the land.
